title: AutoCode: LLMs as Problem Setters for Competitive Programming
claim: A staged closed-loop procedure of creating, generating, validating and stress-testing yields reliable problems and test cases, mirroring expert workflow.
layout: 4 columns, top-to-bottom flow within each, numbered stage headers, orange gradient
description: Four vertical columns headed '1 Create', '2 Generate', '3 Validate', '4 Stress', each in a progressively darker orange. Each column holds three rounded boxes with titled borders, linked by downward black arrows labeled with the operation (Create, Solve, Generator, Generate, Validator w/ tests, Validate, Run, Checker w/ tests). Column 1 goes from a seed problem to a new problem, then to reference and brute-force solutions. Column 2 shows the new problem, a generator program in code, and test cases. Column 3 shows the problem, a validator program with assertions, and validated test cases. Column 4 runs validated tests through the solutions and checks the output, with orange and blue document icons marking the solutions. Orange text highlights the modified problem statement. A short horizontal arrow links the test cases in column 2 to the validated cases in column 3. The eye goes first to the large numbered headers.
caption: AutoCode introduces a closed-loop multi-role Validator-Generator-Checker framework that enables robust test case generation and scalable, self-verified problem generation for competitive programming. It achieves 98.7% consistency with official judgments. This framework precisely mirrors the process human experts follow when creating programming contest problems.
abstract: Writing competitive programming problems is exacting. Authors must: set constraints, input distributions, and edge cases that rule out shortcuts; target specific algorithms (e.g., max-flow, dynamic programming, data structures); and calibrate complexity beyond the reach of most competitors. We argue that this makes for an ideal test of general large language model capabilities and study whether they can do this reliably. We introduce AutoCode, which uses multiple rounds of validation to yield competition-grade problem statements and test cases. On held-out problems, AutoCode test suites approach 99% consistency with official judgments, a significant improvement over current state-of-the-art methods like HardTests, which achieve less than 81%. Furthermore, starting with a random seed problem, AutoCode can create novel variants with reference and brute-force solutions. By cross-verifying these generated solutions against test cases, we can further filter out malformed problems. Our system ensures high correctness, as verified by human experts. AutoCode successfully produces novel problems judged by Grandmaster-level (top 0.3%) competitive programmers to be of contest quality.
